findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: @quackai/q402-mcp
findings.detail: 'quackai__q402-mcp' launches @quackai/q402-mcp through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["@quackai/q402-mcp@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): q402_escrow_status
findings.detail: The description of 'quackai__q402-mcp.q402_escrow_status' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: encoded_blob. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: encoded_blob, entropy, imperative_density.

evidence.description: Read a Q402 escrow's current state (pending/open/disputed/released/refunded/expired) + parties, amount, and tx hashes. Works for escrows on any enabled chain — see GET /api/escrow/chains for the current list.

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description:
Generic x402 client. Fetches any URL with GET/POST and handles x402 payment-required (HTTP 402) responses automatically: parses the x402 v2 payment requirements, validates the payment option (Base USDC only), guards against excess spend, signs an EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization, and retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE (v2 servers) or X-PAYMENT (v1 legacy). Non-402 responses are passed through directly, so this also serves as a regular fetch tool. 

PREREQUISITE — EIP-7702 delegation check: if q402

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'quackai__q402-mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends data outbound
findings.detail: 61 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends data outbound. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send data to an address it controls. A single prompt is enough to turn 'summarise this config' into a credential leak. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'quackai__q402-mcp': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 394 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
